item.text: The 2009 Victorian Bushfires Royal Commission examined the causes of the January and February fires, preparation, emergency response and measures to reduce future risks.
item.support: The Commission was asked to inquire into and report on the causes and circumstances of the fires

item.text: It investigated fifteen fires in detail, including the circumstances of deaths and the operation of bushfire safety policies.
item.support:
the Commission examined in detail 15 fires that caused 
(or had the potential to cause) the greatest damage.

item.text: The Commission concluded that the stay or go policy retained sound principles but did not adequately account for the most severe fires or provide enough alternatives.
item.support: As a result of its inquiries the Commission concludes that the central tenets of the stay or go policy remain sound.

item.text: It also found that divided leadership responsibilities and incompatible agency systems hindered the emergency response.
item.support:
it highlighted serious deficiencies in top-level leadership as a result of divided 
responsibilities

item.text: Its 67 numbered recommendations address safety policy, emergency operations, infrastructure, planning, land management, research and implementation oversight.
item.support: The State appoint an independent monitor or the Victorian Auditor-General to assess progress

item.quote: The 7 February fires did, however, severely test the policy and exposed weaknesses in the way it was applied.
The absolute priority is to improve operational performance.
